SAVED DATA VERIFIED: sizes, CRC32 and GDI layout agree

conclusions: The overlapped DMA engine captured the whole disc in 19.6 minutes at 985.9 KiB/s against 26.7 minutes and 723.5 KiB/s with PIO (Trip 7): +36.3%, 427 s saved, landing on Trip 10's 19.8-minute projection.
Disc time went from 438.8 s to 5.9 s (98.7% hidden). Every other part is unchanged to within a second (SD write 1025.0 s against 1024.9 s), which is what should happen when only the read moves.

Correct by two independent checks: on the console the CRC32 accumulated while reading matches TOSEC on every track, so the DMA read was byte-perfect; on the PC every saved file matches that CRC32 and the reference (REFERENCE MATCH 3/3), so the card wrote it correctly.

Byte-identical by SHA-256 to two earlier captures of the same disc: the 2026-09-17 old-defaults capture (SHA-256, full read-back) and Trip 7 (fast settings, PIO). Three different read paths, one set of bytes.
The SD write is now 87% of a capture and the disc 0.5%: the SD card over SCIF is the whole remaining bottleneck.

limitations: One disc, one card, one console, one capture.
The overlapped read exists only in the experimental build.
